**3 of 4.** Targets `integration/02-nucleos-into-repo`.

Arbor's chain becomes the only one accepting writes. The Nucleos CBAM chain is **sealed, not imported.**

## Why not imported

Arbor's `AuditEntry` is keyed per entity with a gapless sequence. Nucleos's rows are keyed per case, carrying a tenant, and **nothing in either schema maps a Nucleos tenant to an Arbor entity.** Its 25 tenants were sample data.

Importing would have meant attaching audit history to guessed companies — in the one part of the product whose purpose is knowing exactly where a record came from.

Two facts made the simple path available, both confirmed against production before any code was written: no entry ever backed a filed declaration or was shown to a supplier or auditor, and **no case has ever been deleted** (zero orphaned audit rows, zero orphaned snapshots, zero deletion events).

## Why seal at all

Not importing is not the same as pretending the chain never existed.

**A chain that stops with no record of where it stopped is indistinguishable from one that was truncated** — and "entries are missing" is the single accusation this system exists to be able to answer. So its final state is recorded as the origin marker of Arbor's chain.

## What the seal guarantees

It hashes the ordered signatures, so it commits to the whole chain. Altering an entry, reordering two, or removing one each change it — tested individually.

`ForeignChainSeal` is unique by origin and **refuses to be overwritten with a different final state**: that write is the only one that could hide a chain having continued after it was declared closed. Identical re-seals are idempotent, so replaying the handover is safe.

`importedIntoArbor` is stored rather than implied, because a reader has to be able to tell "nothing was imported" from "nobody recorded whether anything was".

The audit package now carries preceding sealed chains. Without them it presents Arbor's chain as though it began from nothing.

## Also here

`N5`: production has **two** audit tables. `cbam.audit_log` (10 rows) is what the application uses; `public.audit_log` (1 pre-CBAM row) is what migration 004 actually altered, because it named the table unqualified. The chain works — it uses `chain_hash` — only the migration was misdirected. 004 is retired as a documented no-op rather than deleted, since it has already run everywhere.

## Review

- Is sealing-without-importing the right call? It is reversible: the seal records enough to import later.
- `ForeignChainSeal` is deliberately not entity-scoped.
